sn44.1:0.1: the tathāgata (here) means a being. This would give the question: Does a being exist (not exist, both exist and not exist, neither exist nor not exist) after death? “Just so, Great King, through knowing whatever bodily form a Realised One can be known by, that form the Realised One has abandoned, cut off at the root, made a palm stump,
sn44.1:0.2: made unviable, so that by nature it is unable to rise again in the future. And the commentary concurs: ‘That form the Tathāgata has abandoned,’ means
sn44.1:1.1: At one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn44.1:1.2: Then at that time the nun Khemā, while walking gradually through Kosala on walking tour, between Sāvatthī and Sāketa, had reached and was dwelling in Toraṇavatthu.
sn44.1:1.3: Then the Kosalan King Pasenadi was going to Sāvatthī from Sāketa and was between Sāvatthī and Sāketa and had reached and was dwelling in Toraṇavatthu for a night.
sn44.1:1.4: Then the Kosalan King Pasenadi addressed a certain man,
sn44.1:1.5: saying: “Please go, dear Sir, and in Toraṇavatthu see if there would be a suitable and knowledgeable ascetic or brāhmaṇa I can pay homage to today.”
sn44.1:2.1: “Yes, your Majesty”, said that man, and after replying to the Kosalan King Pasenadi, and wandering through the whole of Toraṇavatthu, he did not find a suitable and knowledgeable ascetic or brāhmaṇa that the Kosalan King Pasenadi could pay homage to.
sn44.1:2.2: (But) the man did see that the nun Khemā had reached and was dwelling in Toraṇavatthu.
sn44.1:2.3: Having seen (her), he approached the Kosalan King Pasenadi, and after approaching he said this to the Kosalan King Pasenadi:
sn44.1:3.1: “There is not, your Majesty, in Toraṇavatthu a suitable and knowledgeable ascetic or brāhmaṇa your Majesty can pay homage to today.
sn44.1:3.2: But there is, your Majesty, the nun named Khemā, who is a disciple of the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha,
sn44.1:3.3: and about this Noble Lady this beautiful report has gone round:
sn44.1:3.4: ‘She is wise, learned, intelligent, a beautiful orator and extemporary speaker.’
sn44.1:3.5: Your Majesty can pay homage to her.”
sn44.1:4.1: Then the Kosalan King Pasenadi approached the nun Khemā, and after approaching and worshipping the nun Khemā, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side the Kosalan King Pasenadi said this to the nun Khemā:
sn44.1:4.2: “How is it, Noble Lady, does the Realised One exist after death?”
sn44.1:4.3: “This has not been answered, Great King, by the Fortunate One:
sn44.1:4.4: ‘Does the Realised One exist after death?’”
sn44.1:4.5: “But how is it, Noble Lady, does the Realised One not exist after death?”
sn44.1:4.6: “This has not been answered, Great King, by the Fortunate One:
sn44.1:4.7: ‘Does the Realised One not exist after death?’”
sn44.1:4.8: “How is it, Noble Lady, does the Realised One exist and not exist after death?”
sn44.1:4.9: “This has not been answered, Great King, by the Fortunate One:
sn44.1:4.10: ‘Does the Realised One exist and not exist after death?’”
sn44.1:4.11: “But how is it, Noble Lady, does the Realised One neither exist nor not exist after death?”
sn44.1:4.12: “This has not been answered, Great King, by the Fortunate One:
sn44.1:4.13: ‘Does the Realised One neither exist nor not exist after death?’”

sn44.1:6.1: “Now then, Great King, here I will ask you something in return, as you see fit, so you should answer.
sn44.1:6.2: What do you think, Great King,
sn44.1:6.3: do you have a mathematician, or a calculator or an accountant who is able to count the (amount of) sand in the Ganges,
sn44.1:6.4: (saying): there is this much sand, or there are so many hundreds of (grains of) sand, or there are so many thousands of (grains of) sand, or there are so many hundreds of thousands of (grains of) sand?”
sn44.1:6.6: “But do you have a mathematician, or a calculator or an accountant who is able to measure the water in the great ocean,
sn44.1:6.7: (saying): there are this many gallons of water, or there are this many hundreds of gallons of water, or there are this many thousands of gallons of water, or there are this many hundreds of thousands of gallons of water?”
sn44.1:6.9: What is the cause of that?
sn44.1:6.10: Great is the ocean, Noble Lady, deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom.”
sn44.1:6.11: “Just so, Great King, through knowing whatever bodily form a Realised One can be known by, that form the Realised One has abandoned, cut off at the root, made a palm stump, made unviable, so that by nature it is unable to rise again in the future.
sn44.1:6.12: The Realised One, Great King, is free from being considered as bodily form,
sn44.1:6.13: he is deep, immeasurable, hard to fathom, like the great ocean.
sn44.1:6.14: ‘Does the Realised One exist after death?’ does not apply, ‘Does the Realised One not exist after death?’ does not apply, ‘Does the Realised One exist and not exist after death?’ does not apply, ‘Does the Realised One neither exist nor not exist after death?’ does not apply.

sn44.1:9.5: Then the Kosalan King Pasenadi, after greatly rejoicing and gladly receiving this word of the nun Khemā, having worshipped and circumambulated the nun Khemā, departed.

sn44.1:13.1: “It is wonderful, reverend Sir, it is marvellous, reverend Sir,
sn44.1:13.2: in as much as the Teacher and the Disciple agree in the meaning with the meaning and in the letter with the letter, concur, do not contradict, that is to say, in regard to the highest matter.
sn44.1:13.3: On one occasion, reverend Sir, after approaching the nun Khemā, I asked about this matter,
sn44.1:13.4: and the Noble Lady answered this matter for me with this meaning, with this letter, just as the Fortunate One did.
sn44.1:13.5: It is wonderful, reverend Sir, it is marvellous, reverend Sir,
sn44.1:13.6: in as much as the Teacher and the Disciple agree in the meaning with the meaning and in the letter with the letter, concur, do not contradict, that is to say, in regard to the highest matter.
sn44.1:13.7: And now, reverend Sir, we shall go,
sn44.1:13.8: as we have many duties, and there is much which ought to be done.”
sn44.1:13.9: “Now is the time, Great King, for whatever you are thinking.”
sn44.1:13.10: The Kosalan King Pasenadi, after greatly rejoicing and gladly receiving this word of the Fortunate One, having worshipped and circumambulated the Fortunate One, departed.
